newsitem.title: USA: AOL gets hit with another class action suit.
newsitem.headline: AOL gets hit with another class action suit.

text.p: America Online Inc was hit with another class action lawsuit on Wednesday, when a New York law firm filed a suit on behalf of four members and all the AOL subscribers, who are frustrated with AOL's service.

The lawsuit, filed Tuesday in New York State Supreme Court by the law firm of Goodkind Labaton Rudoff & Sucharow LLP, comes on the heels of a class action lawsuit filed in Los Angeles, on behalf of five subscribers, seeking damages for what they call fraudulent and malicious representation.
Since AOL switched its members to unlimited access for $19.95 a month, its network has been deluged by subscribers.

"Anyone who has tried to access AOL and its Internet service recently knows there is an interminably long wait and that the company is not providing what it has promised to its subscribers," said attorney Edward Labaton, in a statement.

"It is particularly damaging to the millions of those who have been promised unlimited access on AOL for $19.95 per month and cannot benefit from the contractual obligation America Online has with them," he continued.
The lawsuit claims breach of contract, unjust enrichment, deceptive trade practices and false advertising by AOL. An AOL spokeswoman said she had not yet seen this suit.

Peter Zinman, an attorney for Goodkind Labaton Rudoff & Sucharow said their lawsuit is separate from the one filed in Los Angeles this week, but the cases could be consolidated into one class action, but it is not certain yet.
"I would predict that there would be many suits filed all over the country," said Zinman.

At least two state attorney generals confirmed they are in discussions with America Online, seeking some resolution to the complaints they have received from consumers about the ongoing problem of network access.

"Attorney General Vacco has initiated discussions with AOL regarding the issue," said a spokesman for the New York State Attorney General Dennis Vacco. "Ultimately, we will determine what the appropriate course of action will be, there may be refunds or something, it is too early to say."
In Wisconsin, the State Attorney General Jim Doyle is also involved in ongoing discussions with AOL, after his office received numerous complaints from consumers.
"Our office, along with a number of states, is involved in ongoing discussions with the company," said a spokesman for the Wisconsin Attorney General's office.
